name: DS18B20 1-Wire temperature sensor
description: Maxim/Analog Devices digital thermometer, -55 to +125 °C (±0.5 °C from -10 to +85 °C), 9-12 bit resolution (0.0625 °C at the default 12 bits), on a 1-Wire bus with a unique 64-bit ROM code per chip. Runs on 3.0-5.5 V. Sold as: KY-001 temperature sensor module (3-pin: S, +, -) with a 4.7 kΩ pull-up from S to + on the board.
eli5: A tiny thermometer that sends the temperature as a number down a single wire; you can hang several on the same wire.

pins.name: S
pins.description: 1-Wire data (DQ); 4.7 kΩ pull-up to + on the module
Supply, 3.0-5.5 V (use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico: the pull-up goes to this pin)

buildNotes: Power the module from 3.3 V when S goes to an ESP32 or Pico: the on-board 4.7 kΩ pull-up ties S to +.
Send Convert T (44h), then wait at least 750 ms (12-bit) before Read Scratchpad (BEh); MicroPython's ds18x20 module does the commands and the CRC check, your code does the wait.
Temperature = signed 16-bit register x 0.0625 °C. A reading of exactly 85 °C is the power-on value: the conversion did not finish or the sensor lost power.
If scan() finds nothing, check the S wire and that + and - are not swapped (a reversed DS18B20 gets hot fast).
Several modules can share one GPIO, but their pull-ups add in parallel: keep at most 2-3 fitted.

example.code:
import machine, onewire, ds18x20, time

ds = ds18x20.DS18X20(onewire.OneWire(machine.Pin({S})))
roms = ds.scan()
print('found', len(roms))
while True:
    ds.convert_temp()
    time.sleep_ms(750)  # 12-bit conversion: up to 750 ms
    print('T=%.2fC' % ds.read_temp(roms[0]))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the temperature set on the slider

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (1 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
